To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CEDL, our new descriptive document clustering method, can discover meaningful clusters and their labels in document collections using a co‐embedded representation of the documents and candidate topics, and that it outperforms the state‐of‐the‐art in the literature.
CEDL is a novel, descriptive clustering framework that can discover semantically interrelated document clusters and their meaningful labels using multilevel similarities.
CEDL is able to discover clusters of semantically related documents together with meaningful descriptive labels, and it is more effective than state‐of‐the‐art methods in the literature.
